user.title: Connect to your Yarbo
user.description: Enter the address of the robot on your network. Nothing leaves your LAN; no Yarbo account is involved.

data_description.host: IP address or DNS name of the robot itself (the rover), for example 192.168.50.184 or yarbo.localdomain. The base station relays the same data and also works.
data_description.port: MQTT port on the robot. 1883 unless you changed it.
data_description.serial: Optional. If this address carries several robots you will be asked which one; enter a serial here to skip the question.
data_description.name: Optional. What to call this robot in Home Assistant. Left empty, it is named Yarbo_ followed by its serial number. You can change it later in the integration's options.
What to call this robot in Home Assistant. You can change it later in the integration's options.

data_description.host: New IP address or DNS name of the robot.

pick_robot.title: Which robot?
pick_robot.description: {host} carries {count} robots ({configured} already set up). Each robot gets its own entry; run this again for the others.

data_description.serial: The serial number is on the label under the robot's rear cover and in the Yarbo app under Device information.

error.cannot_connect: No robot answered at that address. Check that Home Assistant can reach the robot's network and that the robot is powered.
error.wrong_serial: Robots answered at that address, but none has the serial number you entered.

abort.already_configured: This robot is already set up. Its address has been updated.
abort.cannot_connect: The discovered device did not answer as a Yarbo robot.
abort.unique_id_mismatch: That address does not carry this robot. Its serial number was not heard there, so the entry was left alone.
abort.all_configured: Every robot at that address is already set up.

data_description.name: What this robot is called in Home Assistant. The serial number and the entity ids do not change.
data_description.subnet: Optional CIDR such as 192.168.50.0/24. When the robot stops answering at its last address, this subnet is scanned for it. Useful when the robot lives on another VLAN where Home Assistant cannot see DHCP.
data_description.keep_awake: Re-send the wake command every two and a half minutes so telemetry streams continuously. Costs battery while undocked; off by default.

error.invalid_subnet: Enter a subnet in CIDR form, for example 192.168.50.0/24.

entry_not_found.message: No Yarbo Local entry with id {entry_id}.

entry_not_loaded.message: {title} is not loaded. Check that the robot is reachable.

map_unavailable.message: The robot did not return its map: {error}

run_not_found.message: No logged plan run with id {run_id}.

controller_unavailable.message: The robot did not hand over control. Close the Yarbo app on your phone, then try again.

not_verified.message: This integration cannot {action} yet: the command has not been verified on a real robot.

refused_already_returning.message: The robot is already on its way home.

refused_already_docked.message: The robot is already on the dock, charging.

refused_nothing_to_resume.message: No plan is paused, so there is nothing to resume.

refused_returning.message: The robot is on its way home.

refused_rtk_not_ready.message: The robot's RTK position fix is not good enough yet.

refused_no_head.message: No head is attached to the robot.

no_plan_selected.message: No plan is chosen. Pick one in the Plan selector first, then start.

plan_not_found.message: The robot has no plan named '{plan}'. Its plans are: {plans}.

plan_start_failed.message: The robot could not start the plan: {reason}. {hint}

plan_start_unconfirmed.message: The start was sent, but the robot did not begin within a few seconds and gave no reason. Check the Yarbo app.

get_map.name: Get map
get_map.description: Reads the map stored on the robot and returns its areas, pathways, no-go zones and dock as GeoJSON, with a summary of names and sizes.

config_entry_id.name: Robot
config_entry_id.description: The Yarbo whose map to read.

get_obstacles.name: Get obstacles
get_obstacles.description: Returns the obstacles the robot reported during a plan run, in map metres and as GeoJSON. Without a run id, the current or most recent run.

config_entry_id.name: Robot
config_entry_id.description: The Yarbo whose obstacle log to read.

run_id.name: Run
run_id.description: A run id from an earlier response. Leave empty for the current or most recent run.

start_plan.name: Start plan
start_plan.description: Starts one of the robot's plans by name, after the same checks as the Start button. The robot says nothing when it cannot route to the area; the Activity sensor then shows the error.

plan.name: Plan
plan.description: The plan's name as it appears in the Yarbo app.

unreachable.title: {name} has not been heard from for 15 minutes
unreachable.description:
A Yarbo sends a heartbeat every few seconds even while it sleeps, so this is not a robot at rest: it has no power, or it is off the network, or its address changed to one this integration could not find. It was last at {host}.

Check that the robot and its base station have power and that the robot is on Wi-Fi. If its address changed, use Reconfigure on the integration. This notice goes away by itself when the robot is heard again.

plan_cannot_start.title: {name} could not start a plan: {reason}

unverified_firmware.title: {name} runs firmware {firmware}, which has not been checked
unverified_firmware.description:
Every command this integration sends was verified on a real robot first, so far on firmware {verified}. Yours runs {firmware}. Reading will very likely keep working; a control may not, and the robot does not always say so.

If everything works, that is worth knowing: the library's site check writes a report that is safe to share. This notice goes away when the library lists your firmware.
